assignment-id.description: The unique identifier of the classroom assignment.

classroom-id.name: classroom_id
classroom-id.description: The unique identifier of the classroom.

enterprise.name: enterprise
enterprise.description: The slug version of the enterprise name.

configuration-id.name: configuration_id
configuration-id.description: The unique identifier of the code security configuration.

day.name: day
day.description: The day to request data for, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

dependabot-alert-comma-separated-classif.name: classification
dependabot-alert-comma-separated-classif.description:
"A comma-separated list of vulnerability classifications. If specified, only alerts for vulnerabilities with these classifications will be returned.

Can be: `malware`, `general`"

dependabot-alert-comma-separated-states.name: state
dependabot-alert-comma-separated-states.description:
"A comma-separated list of states. If specified, only alerts with these states will be returned.

Can be: `auto_dismissed`, `dismissed`, `fixed`, `open`"

dependabot-alert-comma-separated-severit.name: severity
dependabot-alert-comma-separated-severit.description:
"A comma-separated list of severities. If specified, only alerts with these severities will be returned.

Can be: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`"

dependabot-alert-comma-separated-ecosyst.name: ecosystem
dependabot-alert-comma-separated-ecosyst.description:
"A comma-separated list of ecosystems. If specified, only alerts for these ecosystems will be returned.

Can be: `composer`, `go`, `maven`, `npm`, `nuget`, `pip`, `pub`, `rubygems`, `rust`"

dependabot-alert-comma-separated-package.name: package
dependabot-alert-comma-separated-package.description: A comma-separated list of package names. If specified, only alerts for these packages will be returned.

dependabot-alert-comma-separated-epss.name: epss_percentage
dependabot-alert-comma-separated-epss.description:
CVE Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) percentage. Can be specified as:
- An exact number (`n`)
- Comparators such as `>n`, `<n`, `>=n`, `<=n`
- A range like `n..n`, where `n` is a number from 0.0 to 1.0

Filters the list of alerts based on EPSS percentages. If specified, only alerts with the provided EPSS percentages will be returned.

dependabot-alert-comma-separated-has.name: has
dependabot-alert-comma-separated-has.description:
Filters the list of alerts based on whether the alert has the given value. If specified, only alerts meeting this criterion will be returned.
Multiple `has` filters can be passed to filter for alerts that have all of the values. Currently, only `patch` is supported.

dependabot-alert-comma-separated-assigne.name: assignee
dependabot-alert-comma-separated-assigne.description:
Filter alerts by assignees.
Provide a comma-separated list of user handles (e.g., `octocat` or `octocat,hubot`) to return alerts assigned to any of the specified users.
Use `*` to list alerts with at least one assignee or `none` to list alerts with no assignees.

dependabot-alert-scope.name: scope
dependabot-alert-scope.description: The scope of the vulnerable dependency. If specified, only alerts with this scope will be returned.

dependabot-alert-sort.name: sort
dependabot-alert-sort.description:
The property by which to sort the results.
`created` means when the alert was created.
`updated` means when the alert's state last changed.
`epss_percentage` sorts alerts by the Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) percentage.

enterprise-team.name: enterprise-team
enterprise-team.description: The slug version of the enterprise team name. You can also substitute this value with the enterprise team id.

username.name: username
username.description: The handle for the GitHub user account.

org.name: org
org.description: The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.

team-slug.name: team_slug
team-slug.description: The slug of the team name.

public-events-per-page.name: per_page
public-events-per-page.description: The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

gist-id.name: gist_id
gist-id.description: The unique identifier of the gist.

comment-id.name: comment_id
comment-id.description: The unique identifier of the comment.

labels.name: labels
labels.description: "A list of comma separated label names. Example: `bug,ui,@high`"

plan-id.name: plan_id
plan-id.description: The unique identifier of the plan.

sort.name: sort
sort.description: The property to sort the results by.

owner.name: owner
owner.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

repo.name: repo
repo.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

all.name: all
all.description: If `true`, show notifications marked as read.

participating.name: participating
participating.description: If `true`, only shows notifications in which the user is directly participating or mentioned.

before.name: before
before.description: "Only show notifications updated before the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`."

thread-id.name: thread_id
thread-id.description: The unique identifier of the notification thread. This corresponds to the value returned in the `id` field when you retrieve notifications (for example with the [`GET /notifications` operation](https://docs.github.com/rest/activity/notifications#list-notifications-for-the-authenticated-user)).

since-org.name: since
since-org.description: An organization ID. Only return organizations with an ID greater than this ID.

billing-usage-report-year.name: year
billing-usage-report-year.description: If specified, only return results for a single year. The value of `year` is an integer with four digits representing a year. For example, `2025`. Default value is the current year.

billing-usage-report-month-default.name: month
billing-usage-report-month-default.description: If specified, only return results for a single month. The value of `month` is an integer between `1` and `12`. Default value is the current month. If no year is specified the default `year` is used.

billing-usage-report-day.name: day
billing-usage-report-day.description: If specified, only return results for a single day. The value of `day` is an integer between `1` and `31`. If no `year` or `month` is specified, the default `year` and `month` are used.

billing-usage-report-user.name: user
billing-usage-report-user.description: The user name to query usage for. The name is not case sensitive.

billing-usage-report-model.name: model
billing-usage-report-model.description: The model name to query usage for. The name is not case sensitive.

billing-usage-report-product.name: product
billing-usage-report-product.description: The product name to query usage for. The name is not case sensitive.

budget.name: budget_id
budget.description: The ID corresponding to the budget.

billing-usage-report-month.name: month
billing-usage-report-month.description: If specified, only return results for a single month. The value of `month` is an integer between `1` and `12`. If no year is specified the default `year` is used.

billing-usage-report-repository.name: repository
billing-usage-report-repository.description: The repository name to query for usage in the format owner/repository.

billing-usage-report-sku.name: sku
billing-usage-report-sku.description: The SKU to query for usage.

actions-custom-image-definition-id.name: image_definition_id
actions-custom-image-definition-id.description: Image definition ID of custom image

hosted-runner-id.name: hosted_runner_id
hosted-runner-id.description: Unique identifier of the GitHub-hosted runner.

repository-id.name: repository_id
repository-id.description: The unique identifier of the repository.

visible-to-repository.name: visible_to_repository
visible-to-repository.description: Only return runner groups that are allowed to be used by this repository.

runner-group-id.name: runner_group_id
runner-group-id.description: Unique identifier of the self-hosted runner group.

runner-id.name: runner_id
runner-id.description: Unique identifier of the self-hosted runner.

runner-label-name.name: name
runner-label-name.description: The name of a self-hosted runner's custom label.

variables-per-page.name: per_page
variables-per-page.description: The number of results per page (max 30). For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

subject-digest.name: subject_digest
subject-digest.description: The SHA256 digest of the artifact, in the form `sha256:HEX_DIGEST`.

tool-name.name: tool_name
tool-name.description: The name of a code scanning tool. Only results by this tool will be listed. You can specify the tool by using either `tool_name` or `tool_guid`, but not both.

tool-guid.name: tool_guid
tool-guid.description: The GUID of a code scanning tool. Only results by this tool will be listed. Note that some code scanning tools may not include a GUID in their analysis data. You can specify the tool by using either `tool_guid` or `tool_name`, but not both.

dependabot-alert-comma-separated-artifac.name: artifact_registry_url
dependabot-alert-comma-separated-artifac.description: A comma-separated list of artifact registry URLs. If specified, only alerts for repositories with storage records matching these URLs will be returned.

dependabot-alert-comma-separated-artifac.name: artifact_registry
dependabot-alert-comma-separated-artifac.description:
"A comma-separated list of Artifact Registry name strings. If specified, only alerts for repositories with storage records matching these registries will be returned.

Can be: `jfrog-artifactory`"

dependabot-alert-org-scope-comma-separat.name: has
dependabot-alert-org-scope-comma-separat.description:
Filters the list of alerts based on whether the alert has the given value. If specified, only alerts meeting this criterion will be returned.
Multiple `has` filters can be passed to filter for alerts that have all of the values.

dependabot-alert-comma-separated-runtime.name: runtime_risk
dependabot-alert-comma-separated-runtime.description:
"A comma-separated list of runtime risk strings. If specified, only alerts for repositories with deployment records matching these risks will be returned.

Can be: `critical-resource`, `internet-exposed`, `sensitive-data`, `lateral-movement`"

hook-id.name: hook_id
hook-id.description: The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.

api-insights-min-timestamp.name: min_timestamp
api-insights-min-timestamp.description: "The minimum timestamp to query for stats. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`."

api-insights-max-timestamp.name: max_timestamp
api-insights-max-timestamp.description: "The maximum timestamp to query for stats. Defaults to the time 30 days ago. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`."

api-insights-route-stats-sort.name: sort
api-insights-route-stats-sort.description: The property to sort the results by.

api-insights-api-route-substring.name: api_route_substring
api-insights-api-route-substring.description: Providing a substring will filter results where the API route contains the substring. This is a case-insensitive search.

api-insights-sort.name: sort
api-insights-sort.description: The property to sort the results by.

api-insights-subject-name-substring.name: subject_name_substring
api-insights-subject-name-substring.description: Providing a substring will filter results where the subject name contains the substring. This is a case-insensitive search.

api-insights-user-id.name: user_id
api-insights-user-id.description: The ID of the user to query for stats

api-insights-timestamp-increment.name: timestamp_increment
api-insights-timestamp-increment.description: The increment of time used to breakdown the query results (5m, 10m, 1h, etc.)

api-insights-actor-name-substring.name: actor_name_substring
api-insights-actor-name-substring.description: Providing a substring will filter results where the actor name contains the substring. This is a case-insensitive search.

invitation-id.name: invitation_id
invitation-id.description: The unique identifier of the invitation.

issue-field-id.name: issue_field_id
issue-field-id.description: The unique identifier of the issue field.

issue-type-id.name: issue_type_id
issue-type-id.description: The unique identifier of the issue type.

migration-id.name: migration_id
migration-id.description: The unique identifier of the migration.

role-id.name: role_id
role-id.description: The unique identifier of the role.

package-visibility.name: visibility
package-visibility.description:
The selected visibility of the packages.  This parameter is optional and only filters an existing result set.

The `internal` visibility is only supported for GitHub Packages registries that allow for granular permissions. For other ecosystems `internal` is synonymous with `private`.
For the list of GitHub Packages registries that support granular permissions, see "[About permissions for GitHub Packages](https://docs.github.com/packages/learn-github-packages/about-permissions-for-github-packages#granular-permissions-for-userorganization-scoped-packages)."

package-type.name: package_type
package-type.description: The type of supported package. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. You can use the type `docker` to find images that were pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if these have now been migrated to the Container registry.

package-version-id.name: package_version_id
package-version-id.description: Unique identifier of the package version.

personal-access-token-sort.name: sort
personal-access-token-sort.description: The property by which to sort the results.

personal-access-token-owner.name: owner
personal-access-token-owner.description: A list of owner usernames to use to filter the results.

personal-access-token-repository.name: repository
personal-access-token-repository.description: The name of the repository to use to filter the results.

personal-access-token-permission.name: permission
personal-access-token-permission.description: The permission to use to filter the results.

personal-access-token-before.name: last_used_before
personal-access-token-before.description: "Only show fine-grained personal access tokens used before the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`."

personal-access-token-after.name: last_used_after
personal-access-token-after.description: "Only show fine-grained personal access tokens used after the given time. This is a timestamp in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`."

fine-grained-personal-access-token-id.name: pat_id
fine-grained-personal-access-token-id.description: The unique identifier of the fine-grained personal access token.

field-id.name: field_id
field-id.description: The unique identifier of the field.

item-id.name: item_id
item-id.description: The unique identifier of the project item.

view-number.name: view_number
view-number.description: The number that identifies the project view.

ruleset-targets.name: targets
ruleset-targets.description:
A comma-separated list of rule targets to filter by.
If provided, only rulesets that apply to the specified targets will be returned.
For example, `branch,tag,push`.

ref-in-query.name: ref
ref-in-query.description: The name of the ref. Cannot contain wildcard characters. Optionally prefix with `refs/heads/` to limit to branches or `refs/tags/` to limit to tags. Omit the prefix to search across all refs. When specified, only rule evaluations triggered for this ref will be returned.

repository-name-in-query.name: repository_name
repository-name-in-query.description: The name of the repository to filter on.

time-period.name: time_period
time-period.description:
The time period to filter by.

For example, `day` will filter for rule suites that occurred in the past 24 hours, and `week` will filter for rule suites that occurred in the past 7 days (168 hours).

actor-name-in-query.name: actor_name
actor-name-in-query.description: The handle for the GitHub user account to filter on. When specified, only rule evaluations triggered by this actor will be returned.

rule-suite-result.name: rule_suite_result
rule-suite-result.description: The rule suite results to filter on. When specified, only suites with this result will be returned.

evaluate-status.name: evaluate_status
evaluate-status.description:
The evaluate status to filter on. When specified, only rule suites resulting from rulesets with the specified evaluate status will be returned.
  - `all` - all rule suites will be returned.
  - `active` - only rule suites resulting from rulesets in active (non-evaluate) mode will be returned.
  - `evaluate` - only rule suites resulting from rulesets in evaluate mode will be returned.

rule-suite-id.name: rule_suite_id
rule-suite-id.description:
The unique identifier of the rule suite result.
To get this ID, you can use [GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets/rule-suites](https://docs.github.com/rest/repos/rule-suites#list-repository-rule-suites)
for repositories and [GET /orgs/{org}/rulesets/rule-suites](https://docs.github.com/rest/orgs/rule-suites#list-organization-rule-suites)
for organizations.

secret-scanning-alert-state.name: state
secret-scanning-alert-state.description: Set to `open` or `resolved` to only list secret scanning alerts in a specific state.

secret-scanning-alert-secret-type.name: secret_type
secret-scanning-alert-secret-type.description: A comma-separated list of secret types to return. All default secret patterns are returned. To return generic patterns, pass the token name(s) in the parameter. See "[Supported secret scanning patterns](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/introduction/supported-secret-scanning-patterns#supported-secrets)" for a complete list of secret types.

secret-scanning-alert-exclude-secret-typ.name: exclude_secret_types
secret-scanning-alert-exclude-secret-typ.description: A comma-separated list of secret types to exclude from the results. All default secret patterns are returned except those matching the specified types. Cannot be combined with the `secret_type` parameter. See "[Supported secret scanning patterns](https://docs.github.com/code-security/secret-scanning/introduction/supported-secret-scanning-patterns#supported-secrets)" for a complete list of secret types.

secret-scanning-alert-exclude-providers.name: exclude_providers
secret-scanning-alert-exclude-providers.description:
A comma-separated list of provider slugs to exclude from the results.
Provider slugs use lowercase with underscores (e.g., `github_secret_scanning`, `clojars`).
You can find the provider slug in the `provider_slug` field of each alert.
Cannot be combined with the `providers` parameter.

secret-scanning-alert-providers.name: providers
secret-scanning-alert-providers.description:
A comma-separated list of provider slugs to filter by.
Provider slugs use lowercase with underscores (e.g., `github_secret_scanning`, `clojars`).
You can find the provider slug in the `provider_slug` field of each alert.
Cannot be combined with the `exclude_providers` parameter.

secret-scanning-alert-resolution.name: resolution
secret-scanning-alert-resolution.description: A comma-separated list of resolutions. Only secret scanning alerts with one of these resolutions are listed. Valid resolutions are `false_positive`, `wont_fix`, `revoked`, `pattern_edited`, `pattern_deleted` or `used_in_tests`.

secret-scanning-alert-assignee.name: assignee
secret-scanning-alert-assignee.description: Filters alerts by assignee. Use `*` to get all assigned alerts, `none` to get all unassigned alerts, or a GitHub username to get alerts assigned to a specific user.

assigned-to-user.summary: Filter for alerts assigned to the user "octocat"

secret-scanning-alert-sort.name: sort
secret-scanning-alert-sort.description: The property to sort the results by. `created` means when the alert was created. `updated` means when the alert was updated or resolved.

secret-scanning-pagination-before-org-re.name: before
secret-scanning-pagination-before-org-re.description: A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for events before this cursor. To receive an initial cursor on your first request, include an empty "before" query string.

secret-scanning-pagination-after-org-rep.name: after
secret-scanning-pagination-after-org-rep.description: A cursor, as given in the [Link header](https://docs.github.com/rest/guides/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api#using-link-headers). If specified, the query only searches for events after this cursor.  To receive an initial cursor on your first request, include an empty "after" query string.

secret-scanning-alert-validity.name: validity
secret-scanning-alert-validity.description: A comma-separated list of validities that, when present, will return alerts that match the validities in this list. Valid options are `active`, `inactive`, and `unknown`.

secret-scanning-alert-publicly-leaked.name: is_publicly_leaked
secret-scanning-alert-publicly-leaked.description: A boolean value representing whether or not to filter alerts by the publicly-leaked tag being present.

secret-scanning-alert-multi-repo.name: is_multi_repo
secret-scanning-alert-multi-repo.description: A boolean value representing whether or not to filter alerts by the multi-repo tag being present.

secret-scanning-alert-hide-secret.name: hide_secret
secret-scanning-alert-hide-secret.description: A boolean value representing whether or not to hide literal secrets in the results.

secret-scanning-alert-bypassed.name: is_bypassed
secret-scanning-alert-bypassed.description: A boolean value (`true` or `false`) indicating whether to filter alerts by their push protection bypass status. When set to `true`, only alerts that were created because a push protection rule was bypassed will be returned. When set to `false`, only alerts that were not caused by a push protection bypass will be returned.

network-configuration-id.name: network_configuration_id
network-configuration-id.description: Unique identifier of the hosted compute network configuration.

network-settings-id.name: network_settings_id
network-settings-id.description: Unique identifier of the hosted compute network settings.

team-type.name: team_type
team-type.description: Filter team results by their type. For more information, see "[What kind of team should I use?](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/concepts/enterprise-fundamentals/teams-in-an-enterprise#what-kind-of-team-should-i-use)"

security-product.name: security_product
security-product.description: The security feature to enable or disable.

org-security-product-enablement.name: enablement
org-security-product-enablement.description:
The action to take.

`enable_all` means to enable the specified security feature for all repositories in the organization.
`disable_all` means to disable the specified security feature for all repositories in the organization.

artifact-name.name: name
artifact-name.description: The name field of an artifact. When specified, only artifacts with this name will be returned.

artifact-id.name: artifact_id
artifact-id.description: The unique identifier of the artifact.

actions-cache-git-ref-full.name: ref
actions-cache-git-ref-full.description: The full Git reference for narrowing down the cache. The `ref` for a branch should be formatted as `refs/heads/<branch name>`. To reference a pull request use `refs/pull/<number>/merge`.

actions-cache-key.name: key
actions-cache-key.description: An explicit key or prefix for identifying the cache

actions-cache-list-sort.name: sort
actions-cache-list-sort.description: The property to sort the results by. `created_at` means when the cache was created. `last_accessed_at` means when the cache was last accessed. `size_in_bytes` is the size of the cache in bytes.

actions-cache-key-required.name: key
actions-cache-key-required.description: A key for identifying the cache.

cache-id.name: cache_id
cache-id.description: The unique identifier of the GitHub Actions cache.

concurrency-group-name.name: concurrency_group_name
concurrency-group-name.description: The name of the concurrency group.

job-id.name: job_id
job-id.description: The unique identifier of the job.

actor.name: actor
actor.description: Returns someone's workflow runs. Use the login for the user who created the `push` associated with the check suite or workflow run.

workflow-run-branch.name: branch
workflow-run-branch.description: Returns workflow runs associated with a branch. Use the name of the branch of the `push`.

event.name: event
event.description: Returns workflow run triggered by the event you specify. For example, `push`, `pull_request` or `issue`. For more information, see "[Events that trigger workflows](https://docs.github.com/actions/automating-your-workflow-with-github-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows)."

workflow-run-status.name: status
workflow-run-status.description: Returns workflow runs with the check run `status` or `conclusion` that you specify. For example, a conclusion can be `success` or a status can be `in_progress`. Only GitHub Actions can set a status of `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested`.

created.name: created
created.description: Returns workflow runs created within the given date-time range. For more information on the syntax, see "[Understanding the search syntax](https://docs.github.com/search-github/getting-started-with-searching-on-github/understanding-the-search-syntax#query-for-dates)."

exclude-pull-requests.name: exclude_pull_requests
exclude-pull-requests.description: If `true` pull requests are omitted from the response (empty array).

workflow-run-check-suite-id.name: check_suite_id
workflow-run-check-suite-id.description: Returns workflow runs with the `check_suite_id` that you specify.

workflow-run-head-sha.name: head_sha
workflow-run-head-sha.description: Only returns workflow runs that are associated with the specified `head_sha`.

run-id.name: run_id
run-id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run.

attempt-number.name: attempt_number
attempt-number.description: The attempt number of the workflow run.

workflow-id.name: workflow_id
workflow-id.description: The ID of the workflow. You can also pass the workflow file name as a string.

autolink-id.name: autolink_id
autolink-id.description: The unique identifier of the autolink.

branch.name: branch
branch.description: The name of the branch. Cannot contain wildcard characters. To use wildcard characters in branch names, use [the GraphQL API](https://docs.github.com/graphql).

check-run-id.name: check_run_id
check-run-id.description: The unique identifier of the check run.

check-suite-id.name: check_suite_id
check-suite-id.description: The unique identifier of the check suite.

check-name.name: check_name
check-name.description: Returns check runs with the specified `name`.

status.name: status
status.description: Returns check runs with the specified `status`.

code-quality-finding-number.name: finding_number
code-quality-finding-number.description: The number that identifies a finding.

git-ref.name: ref
git-ref.description: The Git reference for the results you want to list. The `ref` for a branch can be formatted either as `refs/heads/<branch name>` or simply `<branch name>`. To reference a pull request use `refs/pull/<number>/merge`.

pr-alias.name: pr
pr-alias.description: The number of the pull request for the results you want to list.

alert-number.name: alert_number
alert-number.description: The number that identifies an alert. You can find this at the end of the URL for a code scanning alert within GitHub, and in the `number` field in the response from the `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts` operation.

reaction-id.name: reaction_id
reaction-id.description: The unique identifier of the reaction.

commit-ref.name: ref
commit-ref.description: The commit reference. Can be a commit SHA, branch name (`heads/BRANCH_NAME`), or tag name (`tags/TAG_NAME`). For more information, see "[Git References](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-References)" in the Git documentation.

value.body:
# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct

## Our Pledge

In the interest of fostering an open and welcoming environment, we as contributors and maintainers pledge to making participation in our project and our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, disability, ethnicity, gender identity and expression, level of experience, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

## Our Standards

Examples of behavior that contributes to creating a positive environment include:

* Using welcoming and inclusive language
* Being respectful of differing viewpoints and experiences
* Gracefully accepting constructive criticism
* Focusing on what is best for the community
* Showing empathy towards other community members

Examples of unacceptable behavior by participants include:

* The use of sexualized language or imagery and unwelcome sexual attention or advances
* Trolling, insulting/derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
* Public or private harassment
* Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or electronic address, without explicit permission
* Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

## Our Responsibilities

Project maintainers are responsible for clarifying the standards of acceptable behavior and are expected to take appropriate and fair corrective action in response
                  to any instances of unacceptable behavior.

Project maintainers have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, or to ban temporarily or permanently any contributor for other behaviors that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies both within project spaces and in public spaces when an individual is representing the project or its community. Examples of representing a project or community include using an official project e-mail address,
                  posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event. Representation of a project may be further defined and clarified by project maintainers.

## Enforcement

Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported by contacting the project team at [EMAIL]. The project team will review and investigate all complaints, and will respond in a way that it deems appropriate to the circumstances. The project team is obligated to maintain confidentiality with regard to the reporter of an incident. Further details of specific enforcement policies may be posted separately.

Project maintainers who do not follow or enforce the Code of Conduct in good faith may face temporary or permanent repercussions as determined by other members of the project's leadership.

## Attribution

This Code of Conduct is adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](http://contributor-covenant.org), version 1.4, available at [http://contributor-covenant.org/version/1/4](http://contributor-covenant.org/version/1/4/).

items.name: ruby
items.short_description: Ruby is a scripting language designed for simplified object-oriented programming.
items.description: Ruby was developed by Yukihiro "Matz" Matsumoto in 1995 with the intent of having an easily readable programming language. It is integrated with the Rails framework to create dynamic web-applications. Ruby's syntax is similar to that of Perl and Python.

items.name: rails
items.short_description: Ruby on Rails (Rails) is a web application framework written in Ruby.
items.description: Ruby on Rails (Rails) is a web application framework written in Ruby. It is meant to help simplify the building of complex websites.

items.name: python
items.short_description: Python is a dynamically typed programming language.
items.description: Python is a dynamically typed programming language designed by Guido Van Rossum. Much like the programming language Ruby, Python was designed to be easily read by programmers. Because of its large following and many libraries, Python can be implemented and used to do anything from webpages to scientific research.

items.name: jekyll
items.short_description: Jekyll is a simple, blog-aware static site generator.
items.description: Jekyll is a blog-aware, site generator written in Ruby. It takes raw text files, runs it through a renderer and produces a publishable static website.

items.name: sass
items.short_description: Sass is a stable extension to classic CSS.
items.description: Sass is a stylesheet language with a main implementation in Ruby. It is an extension of CSS that makes improvements to the old stylesheet format, such as being able to declare variables and using a cleaner nesting syntax.
items.created_by: Hampton Catlin, Natalie Weizenbaum, Chris Eppstein

items.name: homebrew
items.short_description: Homebrew is a package manager for macOS.
items.description: Homebrew is a package manager for Apple's macOS operating system. It simplifies the installation of software and is popular in the Ruby on Rails community.
